title: Plan Before Search: Search Agents Need Plan

paper.title: Plan Before Search: Search Agents Need Plan
paper.abstract: Abstract Training large language models as retrieval-augmented reasoning agents typically combines reinforcement learning with an SFT cold start distilled from a stronger model. However, this paradigm overlooks two fundamental factors: the dependency structure among sub-skills, and the possibility that distillation is not the only route to capability acquisition. We study this through Plan, a structured agentic behavior for multi-hop retrieval that decomposes a question into ordered sub-questions before any retrieval is performed, so that each search step can be anchored to a pre-designed sub-question instead of drifting under the influence of partially relevant documents retrieved earlier. However, across three model families spanning 3B to 14B parameters, we find that an identical reward signal induces qualitatively different RL failure modes. This phenomenon indicates that successful training hinges not only on reward design but also on model-specific feasibility conditions: sufficient initial entropy, training stability, and prerequisite sub-skills. Motivated by this, we propose a self-bootstrapping paradigm in which a small-scale seed model generates filtered trajectories that activate Plan in any target model, eliminating the need for distillation from an external stronger model. Our pipeline activates Plan across every tested model and consistently outperforms competitive baselines on multi-hop QA benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/qzp2018/PL-Search .

Corresponding author Abstract Training large language models as retrieval-augmented reasoning agents typically combines reinforcement learning with an SFT cold start distilled from a stronger model. However, this paradigm overlooks two fundamental factors: the dependency structure among sub-skills, and the possibility that distillation is not the only route to capability acquisition. We study this through Plan, a structured agentic behavior for multi-hop retrieval that decomposes a question into ordered sub-questions before any retrieval is performed, so that each search step can be anchored to a pre-designed sub-question instead of drifting under the influence of partially relevant documents retrieved earlier. However, across three model families spanning 3B to 14B parameters, we find that an identical reward signal induces qualitatively different RL failure modes. This phenomenon indicates that successful training hinges not only on reward design but also on model-specific feasibility conditions: sufficient initial entropy, training stability, and prerequisite sub-skills. Motivated by this, we propose a self-bootstrapping paradigm in which a small-scale seed model generates filtered trajectories that activate Plan in any target model, eliminating the need for distillation from an external stronger model. Our pipeline activates Plan across every tested model and consistently outperforms competitive baselines on multi-hop QA benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/qzp2018/PL-Search . 1 Introduction Figure 1: Comparison with traditional search agents. (a) Our method first generates a global plan that decomposes the question into ordered sub-questions; each subsequent search is anchored to one sub-question, yielding the correct answer. (b) Without a plan, the agent forms each search query reactively from previously retrieved results, and the query progressively drifts from the original question, leading to a wrong answer. Recent work has demonstrated that reinforcement learning can effectively train large language models to acquire search-augmented reasoning behaviors. Search-R1 ( Jin et al., 2025 ) pioneers training models via RL to interleave thinking and retrieval within a single trajectory, using outcome-based rewards, and AutoRefine ( Shi et al., 2025 ) extends this framework by introducing explicit document refinement and retrieval-specific rewards. Other works, such as ReSearch ( Chen et al., 2026b ) , further investigate reward shaping and self-reflection mechanisms. When direct RL training proves insufficient for more complex behaviors, a now-standard remedy is to apply supervised fine-tuning as a cold start prior to RL optimization, typically using trajectories distilled from a stronger model. Together, careful reward design and SFT cold start with stronger-model distillation constitute the dominant toolkit for training search-augmented LLMs. However, this paradigm overlooks two aspects of complex agentic behaviors: the role of sub-skill interdependencies in constraining trainability, and whether stronger-model distillation is truly necessary for SFT cold-start. In this paper, we investigate both questions through the plan behavior, since the plan is particularly suited for this investigation for two reasons. First, it sits at the next level of complexity beyond Search-R1 and AutoRefine, requiring the coordination of multiple sub-skills that prior work has addressed individually. Second, without an upfront decomposition of the question, each search step in prior methods largely relies on the documents retrieved in previous steps to decide what to search next. Noisy or partially relevant documents accumulate along the trajectory, causing the agent to drift away from the original question. Figure 1 contrasts this reactive baseline (b) with our plan-based approach (a). A global plan, formulated before any retrieval is performed, anchors each subsequent reasoning step to a fixed sub-question, preventing such drift. We formalize plan as a structured agentic behavior and design a plan-aware reward function that supervises both its structural validity and the alignment between each reasoning step and its planned sub-question. Through systematic experiments across three model families (Qwen2.5, Llama3.2, and Qwen3) and scales ranging from 3B to 14B, we report two findings. First, direct RL training of plan fails in qualitatively different ways across models , despite identical reward designs. Models with low initial entropy lack sufficient exploration room, and the policy cannot acquire new behaviors regardless of the reward signal. In addition, some models train stably at first but collapse abruptly. As entropy rises, output format breaks down, the reward signal vanishes, and training destabilizes irreversibly. Models that lack the refine sub-skill also fail: Plan demands that pre-formulated sub-questions remain consistent with subsequently retrieved evidence. Without the ability to integrate information across this boundary, both forcing the model to acquire plan and refine simultaneously and forcing it to learn plan first lead to training collapse. Although these failures appear different on the surface, they share a single root cause—the initial model does not satisfy the implicit conditions required for plan RL: room to explore, training stability, and the prerequisite sub-skills. A single SFT pass addresses all three conditions at once, which is why it is effective across all the tested models. Second, we propose a self-bootstrapping training paradigm. Prior work constructs cold-start SFT data by distilling trajectories from a larger and more capable model. We identify an alternative and effective approach: A small seed model that satisfies the feasibility conditions identified above can acquire a plan through direct RL and generate trajectories that activate a plan in any other target model, and the self-bootstrapped data even outperform strong-model distillation in our experiments. Specifically, some models, exemplified by Qwen2.5-3B-Base, can autonomously acquire the plan through pure RL by first learning refinement and then learning plan on top of it. We exploit such a model as a seed that generates plan trajectories, which are then filtered through a quality-aware pipeline and used as SFT data to activate the plan capability in any target model. Through this procedure, every target model, regardless of family or scale, successfully acquires plan and achieves consistent performance gains on multi-hop benchmarks, without the need for an external stronger model. We refer to the resulting method as PL-Search. In summary, our contributions are as follows. • We formulate plan as a structured agentic behavior that prevents trajectory drift by anchoring each retrieval step to a pre-designed sub-question and name it PL-Search, a method trained with a plan-aware reward that supervises step-level sub-question alignment. • We identify three feasibility conditions for direct plan RL—sufficient initial entropy, training stability, and the presence of prerequisite sub-skills—and show that the violation of these conditions manifests as qualitatively distinct failure modes across model families. • We propose a self-bootstrapping paradigm in which a small-scale seed model generates filtered trajectories to activate plan in any target model, eliminating the need for strong-model distillation while outperforming it. 2 Related Work 2.1 RL Training of Agentic LLMs The search field Zheng et al. (2025b) ; Chen et al. (2026a) ; Liang et al. (2025) ; Qian et al. (2026) ; Liang et al. (2026b) ; Liu et al. (2026a) ; Liang et al. (2026a) has witnessed the rapid development of search agents. Search-R1 Jin et al. (2025) established the paradigm of RL-trained agentic search with outcome-based rewards. Subsequent work extended this paradigm through richer reward designs and algorithmic variants, including refinement-augmented trajectories Shi et al. (2025) , tighter integration between reasoning and retrieval Chen et al. (2026b) ; Song et al. (2025) ; Li et al. (2026) , step-wise credit assignment Wang et al. (2025) , retrieval-gain optimization Jiang et al. (2025) , and hierarchical reasoning structures Xu et al. (2026) . When direct RL proves insufficient for more complex behaviors, SFT cold-start with stronger-model distillation has become the default remedy. It is applied in some works Song et al. (2025) ; Sun et al. (2025b) ; Christianos et al. (2023) but skipped in others Jin et al. (2025) ; Chen et al. (2026b) ; Shi et al. (2025) ; Wang et al. (2025) , without a principled understanding of when it is necessary or why it is effective. We use plan to fill this gap: by tracing RL failures to dependencies on prerequisite sub-skills, we explain why SFT cold-start is so consistently effective; and by showing that a small-scale seed model suffices, we demonstrate that stronger-model distillation is not a prerequisite. 2.2 Multi-Step Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Prior work on multi-step retrieval has focused primarily on pipeline design—teaching models to invoke search iteratively through SFT, or enabling adaptive query generation through RL Jin et al. (2025) ; Chen et al. (2026b) ; Zheng et al. (2025a) ; Wang et al. (2025) ; Yuan et al. (2025) ; Wang et al. (2026) ; Feng et al. (2026) ; Tian et al. (2026) , with some approaches incorporating structural elements such as refinement steps Shi et al. (2025) ; Zhao et al. (2025) ; Liu et al. (2026b) ; Zhang et al. (2025a) . The question of how a single model acquires decomposition, retrieval, and integration as jointly dependent sub-skills through RL, and what determines whether that acquisition succeeds, has not yet been addressed. Moreover, in the absence of upfront decomposition, each search query is formed reactively from previously retrieved documents, which accumulates noise and causes trajectories to drift. We study plan as a composite agentic behavior situated at this intersection, using it as a structured probe into the sub-skill dependencies that govern the acquisition of capabilities through RL. Figure 2: Overview of our framework. Given a user question, the policy model first generates a global plan decomposing the question into sub-questions, then iteratively executes think, search, and refine for each sub-question before producing the final answer. Training is driven by a composite reward combining plan, format, and outcome rewards, with the loss masked over retrieved documents. 3 Methodology This section presents our method for studying the prerequisite dependencies of complex agentic behaviors through plan.
